description: The Ground Heat Exchanger Design Tool is a Python package for sizing borehole fields under land and thermal constraints. It computes long-term response functions with pygfunction, then simulates monthly heat-pump entering-fluid temperatures over a design life while varying borehole count, depth or placement. Users supply thermal loads, ground properties, land polygons and temperature limits; outputs are proposed borehole layouts and predicted fluid-temperature paths. Geographic coverage is the selected project site. BSD-3-Clause source, pip installation, examples and a design thesis are public. A limitation is that results depend on ground thermal properties and load forecasts, while drilling permissions and costs require separate evidence. The tool can compare ground-source heat designs for buildings or district heating. The related catalogue GEOPHIRES-X simulates geothermal energy at another scale, not this building borehole layout. No site data or Python package was downloaded.
inputs: Thermal loads, ground properties and site polygons
